subject: research/simdesign-robustmove
professional: a structural-optimisation researcher who runs density-based robust topology optimisation (Wang-Lazarov-Sigmund eroded/blueprint/dilated, SIMP, MMA and OC) and designs numerical studies of optimiser behaviour; first checks: does the FE and projection reproduce independently, is the claimed cause separated from trajectory sensitivity by perturbing the run (neighbouring move limits, iteration counts), is the OC-on-min-max set-up standard or an artefact, and what do Wang et al. 2011 and the later educational codes already say about continuation and move limits

evidence.correctness: The numbers are right. Reran all 18 60x20 runs (scratchpad rerun.py, /usr/bin/python3.13 with numpy/scipy 1.18.1): every c_e, c_b, c_d, spike count and max ratio matches experiments/results.txt to the printed digit. Independent recomputation in scratchpad indep.py, sharing no FE code with the author: Q4 plane-stress stiffness by 2x2 Gauss quadrature from the B-D-B integral (textbook, Cook et al.), matching the closed-form KE to 1.1e-16; own assembly with a different node numbering (row-major from the bottom) and own half-MBB boundary conditions; own cone filter written from Sigmund 2001; own tanh projection written from the Wang, Lazarov and Sigmund 2011 formula. For 60x20, r = 3: move 0.2 gives c_e 1347.3, c_b 741.88, c_d 474.09 and move 0.05 gives 224.0 / 200.29 / 169.49, identical to results.txt; blueprint volume 0.5000 in both. Failure verdicts recomputed by awk from results.txt (c_b > 1.5x the case minimum): 5/9 FAIL at 0.20, 0/9 at 0.10 and 0.05, no mismatch with the status column. The r = 3, move 0.2 history recomputed: about 238-265 through beta = 32, then 918 and 45 567 at iterations 182-183 (three iterations into beta = 64), back to 265, 2 366, ending near 1 200, as the README says. Exploratory claim reproduced: 60 iterations per beta at move 0.2 gives blueprint 203.5.
evidence.completeness: Everything the README lists runs: 6 tests pass (1.17 s); the 18 60x20 rows reproduce exactly (8-10 s each, consistent with the 15-minute total once the 120x40 rows at about 75 s are added; the 120x40 rows were not rerun); history.png exists (990x374 PNG). The 60-iteration exploratory number reproduces; the x1.5 beta-ramp number (568) was not rerun. Limitations and next steps are listed as not done rather than claimed. Live page not loaded (curl to marisstella.app returned no response through the proxy); the homepage summary in research/_homepage/projects.json:2307 matches the README numbers.
evidence.verification: `cd research/simdesign-robustmove && /usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q tests`: 6 passed in 1.17 s. Nine mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (spike max -> mean, inverted ratio, move argument ignored), 6 survived: D_EVAL 0.2 -> 0.1 (the re-analysis thresholds), > -> >= in failed(), MOVES (0.2, 0.1, 0.05) -> (0.2, 0.15, 0.1), the evaluation penalty 3.0 -> 1.0 (changes every reported compliance), c_b returned as the eroded compliance (the headline column), and run.py taking the best over c_e instead of c_b. No test pins any compliance value, against results.txt or against an independent FE value, so the reported table is guarded only by the author rerunning the script.
evidence.craft: Read src/simdesign_robustmove/__init__.py (40 lines), tests/test_move.py, experiments/run.py, and the imported simdesign-robust/robust.py, simdesign-heaviside/proj.py, simdesign-topopt/simp.py. Small and readable, the evaluation reuses the upstream code unchanged as claimed. Defects: the package mutates sys.path at import to reach four sibling projects (__init__.py:9) and pyproject.toml declares none of them, so `pip install` of this project gives an unimportable package; spikes() raises on a history of length 1 (empty ratio, .max()); the OC bisection it calls divides by l1 + l2 and crashed with ZeroDivisionError after NaN overflow for 60x20, r = 4, move 0.25 (simdesign-robust/robust.py:46), with no guard or message.
evidence.claims: Backed by files: every table value, the failure counts (4/6 and 1/3), the blueprint range 193-237 for the 18 small-move runs, '1 to 4 spikes, up to 50x and 409x', the single 7.1x spike at move 0.1, the <3% blueprint difference where 0.2 worked, the eroded 9 762 at r = 5 move 0.1, the reproduction of simdesign-robustmesh's 741.9 and 746.7 (its results.txt:9, :11), '6 tests', and the honest statement that the mechanism is untested. Not backed: the headline 'the cause is the move limit of 0.2' (README.md:3) and the framing of a cliff 'between 0.1 and 0.2' to be located (README.md:50, :54). My perturbation runs show the outcome is not monotone in the move limit and flips on an arbitrary schedule change: at r = 3, moves 0.15, 0.19, 0.20 and 0.25 fail (440.9, 476.6, 741.9, 450.8) while 0.18 and 0.21 pass (201.2, 203.2); at r = 4, 0.15 and 0.19 fail (386.5, 985.1); and at move 0.2, r = 3, 31 iterations per beta passes (201.8) while 29 fails (519.3). 'No seeds exist to vary since the code is deterministic' (README.md:47) is the wrong reason not to perturb: a deterministic run can be perturbed, and doing so changes the verdict. 'More iterations can mask the problem' (README.md:38) reads the 60-iteration result as masking when one extra iteration does the same.
evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher wants to know which OC settings make this robust formulation reliable and build on it (simdesign-robustadapt already did). They get a reproducible, deterministic script and correct numbers, and the practical advice (a move of 0.1 or less) held in every probe I ran: 13 further runs at moves 0.06 to 0.12 on r = 3, 3.5, 4, 5 all passed. What they cannot build on is the causal story: the result is one trajectory per cell, and the verdict at 0.2 is a coin flip under a one-iteration change, so 'locate the threshold' (the next step) is chasing a boundary that does not exist in that form. Nearest prior work: Wang, Lazarov and Sigmund 2011 (the formulation itself, which discusses continuation and convergence and solves the min-max with MMA in a bound formulation; the README says its convergence advice was not checked); Guest, Asadpoure and Ha 2011 and Li and Khandelwal 2015 on projection continuation; Ferrari and Sigmund 2020 (top99neo), whose educational code uses a smaller OC move limit with projection (cited from memory, not re-checked). Instability of OC with steep projection and a large move limit is practitioner knowledge; the result is a modest, expected observation, not new, and it is not compared with any of these.
evidence.domain: Against robust-topology-optimisation practice: Wang et al. 2011 pose min max(c_e, c_b, c_d) as a bound formulation solved with MMA and put the volume constraint on the dilated design (rescaled so the blueprint hits the target); this chain drives the non-smooth max of three with the OC heuristic on the gradient of whichever realisation is active and constrains the blueprint volume. The period-2 oscillation visible in the r = 3 history before the failure (259, 251, 260, 249 ...) is the signature of OC on a switching max. The study does not test whether the failure is an OC-on-min-max artefact (no MMA or bound-formulation comparison), does not perturb the trajectory, and judges a robust design by its blueprint only. A senior optimisation researcher would accept the numbers and the 'use a smaller move' advice, not the causal claim, and would not sign this off at the PhD bar in research/CLAUDE.md.

defects.what: The headline causal claim does not survive perturbation. 'The cause is the move limit of 0.2' and the planned search for a cliff between 0.1 and 0.2 assume a monotone threshold, but at 60x20 r = 3 moves 0.15 and 0.19 fail (440.9, 476.6) while 0.18 and 0.21 pass (201.2, 203.2), at r = 4 0.15 and 0.19 fail, and at move 0.2 one more iteration per beta (31) rescues the run (201.8) while one fewer (29) fails (519.3). The failure is trajectory sensitivity of OC at beta 64 for moves of about 0.15 and above, not a property of 0.2; only 'moves of 0.12 or less were stable' is supported.

One deterministic trajectory per cell, justified by 'no seeds exist to vary since the code is deterministic'; no perturbation (neighbouring move limits, iteration counts, initial design) was run, though such perturbations flip the verdict. No comparison with MMA / the bound formulation Wang et al. 2011 use, so an OC-on-switching-max artefact (period-2 oscillation visible before the failure) is not ruled out; prior work on projection continuation and OC move limits is not compared.

Tests pin no reported number: changing the evaluation penalty 3.0 -> 1.0, returning the eroded compliance as c_b, changing the re-analysis thresholds, the MOVES list, the failure comparison, or run.py's best-of column all leave the 6 tests green (6 of 9 mutants survive).

'More iterations can mask the problem' reads the 60-iteration rescue as masking, when 31 iterations per beta rescues the same run; the exploratory paragraph draws a conclusion ('the move limit did') from single runs.

The package reaches four sibling projects by inserting relative paths into sys.path at import and declares none of them in pyproject.toml, so it cannot be installed and imported on its own; spikes() raises on a one-element history.
The OC bisection divides by l1 + l2 and crashes with ZeroDivisionError after a NaN overflow (60x20, r = 4, move 0.25) instead of reporting a diverged run; reached through run_move.

verdict: The arithmetic is right and reproduces: an independent FE (Gauss-quadrature Q4, own assembly and boundary conditions), own filter and own projection reproduce results.txt to the printed digit for 60x20 r = 3 at moves 0.2 and 0.05, all 18 60x20 rows rerun identically, and the counts and history narrative check out. It does not meet the bar. Verification is 1 (6 of 9 mutants survive, including the evaluation penalty and the headline c_b column), and the main finding is overclaimed: the outcome is not monotone in the move limit (0.15 and 0.19 fail, 0.18 and 0.21 pass at r = 3) and at move 0.2 a one-iteration change to the schedule flips failure to success, so 'the cause is the move limit of 0.2' and the cliff to be located are not supported; what is supported is that moves of 0.12 or less were stable in every run (13 extra probes). As robust topology optimisation it drives a min-max with OC rather than the MMA bound formulation of the paper it builds on and compares with no prior work on continuation or move limits, so a structural-optimisation researcher would accept the numbers and the practical advice, not the causal claim.
